display.purpose: Source Serif 4 page titles for Latin/Cyrillic; regional Noto Serif for zh-Hans, zh-Hant and ja. The Bodoni homepage wordmark has separate fixed-pixel identity sizing.

headline.purpose: Locale-specific editorial serif headings with explicit responsive steps, separate from the MOFER identity marks.

title.purpose: Shared sans-serif h3 baseline; featured objects and exhibition titles use component-specific display typography.

body.purpose: Main reading copy uses Source Sans 3 for en/fr/de/es/ru and Noto Sans SC/TC/JP for the corresponding CJK locale. Reading measures and leading follow the script; hero copy, controls and captions keep component exceptions. Supported families and runtime samples do not establish universal glyph coverage.

label.purpose: Object type and exhibition status below a title, never a before-title kicker.

navigation.purpose: Desktop route labels can wrap at enlarged text sizes; the compact disclosure uses its own larger label size.

collection-title.purpose: Compact object names preceding type metadata in selectable thumbnails.

identityProvenance.status: Existing Moving Archive identity, refined to quiet editorial galleries; no replacement identity or new approval is implied.

fontDelivery.files: Package index.css, LICENSE copied as LICENSE.txt, and every supplied -wght-normal.woff2 file for each family.
fontDelivery.delivery: Local normal-variable faces retain Fontsource unicode-range subsets and font-display: swap. No runtime CDN or custom character subsetting.
fontDelivery.legacy: Committed assets/fonts are excluded from the build copy. The remaining Hanken development dependency is not a generated family or public type role.
fontDelivery.coverageScope: Source includes Cyrillic and Noto uses regional SC/TC/JP families. Family routing and checked runtime samples do not certify every character, fallback environment or native translation.

motion.name: state-feedback
motion.purpose: Navigation background and text, thumbnail opacity, and action-arrow movement.

motion.name: image-feedback
motion.purpose: Image opacity feedback on inspection triggers.

motion.name: hero-arrival
motion.purpose: Homepage content only, at min-width 961px with no reduced-motion preference; not a global entrance recipe.

motion.name: ambient-film-rate
motion.purpose: Both defaultPlaybackRate and playbackRate on the muted, inline, looping film; no on-page playback controls. The film remains visible and requests playback regardless of motion preference; autoplay denial keeps a still fallback.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Disable decorative interface animation and transitions and make scrolling immediate without hiding or pausing the explicitly requested ambient film.

textures.name: archive-paper
textures.purpose: Paper grain from the letter's blank margin, with uneven illumination removed, contrast limited and the crop mirrored. Used on body, masthead, exhibition and footer backgrounds, never on original object photographs. This is derived raster texture, not an AI-generated historical artifact.

narrative.overview:
MOFER's original photographs, documents and film lead a quiet editorial museum. The established porcelain-blue palette, pale-blue actions, muted purple exhibition field and real paper grain remain. Intact objects sit directly in open layouts, with deliberate whitespace instead of repeated colored mats or enclosing panels.

Locale-specific serif headings and sans-serif reading text give eight languages a shared, legible hierarchy. Names lead, full historical context follows, and small factual notes remain in context. The MOFER wordmark over the original film anchors the identity; artifacts and their stories guide visitors through the museum.
keyCharacteristics: Unchanged porcelain-blue fields, pale-blue actions and muted purple exhibitions.
Original paper grain around contained, untextured historical images.
Script-specific reading typography, title-first context and deliberate whitespace.
Six dedicated pages with English fallback and eight persistent language choices.
Original quarter-speed film; reduced motion removes decorative UI movement.

rules.name: The Quiet Accent Rule
rules.body: Pale blue marks actions, selection and keyboard focus against dark surfaces; it does not recolor the historical media.

rules.name: The Script Before Style Rule
rules.body: Use the locale's Source or regional Noto pair for readable text; reserve Bodoni for MOFER identity lettering.

rules.name: The Title First Rule
rules.body: Give headings and object names priority; place classification and exhibition status below them.

rules.name: The Context Before Count Rule
rules.body: Keep quantities, dates and location facts inside compact labelled notes, not oversized standalone statistics.

rules.name: The Open Gallery Rule
rules.body: Give intact objects and their context space; do not restore colored thumbnail mats or an enclosing collection-detail panel.

rules.name: The Flat Gallery Rule
rules.body: Use tonal fields, subtle paper grain and spacing for depth; keep texture off original object photographs and avoid imitation bevels.

dos: Do keep original object images fully visible and free of texture overlays.
Do place names and headings before type and status metadata.
Do use deliberate responsive whitespace and let all eight languages wrap naturally.
Do use the locale-specific font pair and enlarge readable text independently of graphic identity marks.
Do retain full contextual facts and original meaning while improving text allocation.
Do keep the native language select and explicit preference persistence across dedicated pages.
Do retain visible focus, labelled controls, dialog focus return and motion-preference fallbacks.
Do use build-generated local fonts, existing Lucide icons and original historical media.
donts: Don't add white canvases, decorative dividing lines or above-title kickers.
Don't turn sections into floating cards or add bevels, offset shadows or pill controls.
Don't restore colored image mats or an enclosing collection-detail panel.
Don't replace contextual museum notes with giant standalone numbers or crop documents to fill frames.
Don't add visible film playback controls or promise autoplay when the browser blocks it.
Don't hide or pause the requested film for reduced motion; remove decorative UI animation instead.
Don't invent historical evidence, visitor services or approval and rights claims.
Don't publish upcoming-exhibition placeholders or treat a future poster proposal as a shipped pattern.
Don't use wordmark-sized type in compact controls or scale fonts with viewport width.
Don't replace Lucide icons with glyphs or treat sidecar tonal ramps as site colors.
Don't treat legacy source fonts, borrowed museum branding or failed reference captures as current design authority.
